narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 69.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the admissions process uses this prediction as a key factor, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking in the third year of law school was the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting failure. Standing in the bottom decile, far below the average of accepted students (around the 6th decile), signaled to the model that you would likely struggle on the bar. Your first-year ranking in the second decile also contributed to the negative outlook, though less strongly.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.00 worked in the opposite direction. While this value is modestly below the 3.23 average of accepted students, the model still saw it as a mildly positive signal that slightly reduced the predicted risk of failure. However, this encouraging element was not enough to offset the impact of your law-school performance.

Taken together, the model concluded that the risk of bar failure was too high for admission. 

To improve your chances, focus on raising your class standing in the remaining part of your program and consider targeted bar-preparation resources that address the specific gaps reflected in your decile rankings. Reapplying with a stronger academic trajectory could meaningfully change the outcome. (218 words)
